stem: Why is a single universal dryback percentage inappropriate for every crop?
choices: Dryback meaning depends on media properties, container volume, root development, growth stage, environment, irrigation strategy, and plant demand.
A universal percentage can work if all rooms use the same nutrient EC, because EC is the main driver of water use.
A calibrated moisture sensor makes a universal biological dryback target valid across crops because the sensor removes media differences.
Container size matters early in the crop but becomes negligible after the root system fills the substrate.
rationale: Dryback is a pattern of water loss, not a universal biological target. The same percentage can represent very different plant and root-zone conditions depending on substrate water-holding characteristics, container geometry, root occupancy, stage, environment, and irrigation frequency. Calibration improves measurement accuracy, but it does not make one target biologically appropriate for every crop context.
